$comment: One object per case; `skills` names what should load, `expected_behavior` lists what a passing run must do.

routing.query: Our test suite takes four minutes in CI: every test builds a fresh git repository and spawns the CLI, and the whole suite runs in two different jobs. How should we reorganise it?
expected_behavior: loads craft:test-suite-design, not craft:testing-principles alone
gives each check a size and moves rule checks in-process, keeping one spawned smoke per observable outcome
builds the repository template once and copies it per test
runs each test file in exactly one check, so the suite stops running twice
leaves runner idioms to the runner skill and workflow syntax to tooling:github-actions-conventions

routing.query: Every pull request goes red because the README says '585 tests across 74 files' and a check reruns the whole suite to recount them
expected_behavior: loads craft:test-suite-design and applies the change-detector rule of craft:testing-principles §2 that its §5 points to
takes the exact count out of the README: a command prints it, or the figure is dated where it is written
deletes the recount along with the number, rather than swapping it for a static count that still makes every pull request edit the README

routing.query: Four tests each run the same five-second npm install in a sandbox, and each one checks a different fact about the result
expected_behavior: loads craft:test-suite-design
runs the install once and asserts every fact on that one result
keeps a fresh fixture only for a test that needs a different input

routing.query: My node --test file reports every test as passed, then the process only exits about 30 seconds later
expected_behavior: loads node-test:node-test-conventions for the runner mechanics and craft:test-suite-design for the leak rule
looks for a timer or a child process the tests started and never ended
fixes the leak instead of adding an option that forces the run to exit

routing.query: Our nightly canary job in GitHub Actions has been red for three weeks and nobody noticed
expected_behavior: loads craft:test-suite-design for what makes a canary worth having and tooling:github-actions-conventions for the scheduled job
makes a failed run open or update an issue a person reads
routes the canary through the same entry point, and so the same setup, as the gate

routing.query: Add timeout-minutes and a concurrency group to our GitHub Actions workflow
expected_behavior: loads tooling:github-actions-conventions, not craft:test-suite-design
sizes each timeout-minutes from the job's measured durations
cancels superseded pull-request runs only, never a push to main or a scheduled run

routing.query: Is this test any good? It computes the expected total the same way the code does, and it is named after the discount rule
expected_behavior: loads craft:testing-principles, not craft:test-suite-design
flags the tautological assertion and asks for an expected value from an independent source

routing.query: Write a bash test suite for this PreToolUse hook script so each pattern it blocks has its own case
expected_behavior: loads shell-test:shell-test-conventions, not craft:test-suite-design
runs the hook through its hooks.json entry and asserts stdout and stderr apart

routing.query: This hook script uses mapfile and declare -A, and it breaks on the Mac's /bin/bash
expected_behavior: loads mac:mac-platform, not craft:test-suite-design
rewrites both constructs in a form bash 3.2 accepts
